physical_parsing.volume_method: Bell approximated as a hemi-ellipsoid (2/3 * pi * r^2 * h) with r = 0.125 m and h = 0.07 m (dome height above the margin). Upper-bound estimate; the bell is mostly water and the tentacles/oral arms are excluded. The full bounding box is 0.25 x 0.10 x 0.25 m = 0.00625 m^3.
physical_parsing.shape_class: Oblate hemi-ellipsoid (flattened dome / umbrella), radially symmetric, swims bell-first with +Y toward the apex

core.description: Gelatinous bell (umbrella) of mesoglea, mostly water, with a subumbrellar cavity beneath. The central manubrium hangs from the subumbrellar floor. The bell is the body; it is not a rigid skeleton.
core.cross_section: Circular in plan view; dome-shaped in side profile, thickened at the apex and thin at the margin

physical_parsing.size_source: Typical adult bell diameter of about 0.25 m (range roughly 0.1 to 0.4 m), from general marine biology references for Aurelia aurita (for example the Wikipedia species article). NOT retrieved in this session: the Wikipedia and Commons hosts were unreachable, so treat the size as unverified until checked.

parts.name: Bell margin (coronal muscle band)

penetration.overlap_region: Bell margin rim, a circumferential band in the outer mesoglea; the coronal muscle is a thin ring in the subumbrella

parts.notes: The coronal muscle contracts the bell margin to expel water and drive pulsation (jet propulsion). It is an annular ring, not a limb. length_m is the ring circumference (2 pi r). No PolyForge equivalent. Contraction is continuous, not hinged. Bell pulsation is a hydrostatic mechanism.

parts.name: Marginal tentacles

penetration.overlap_region: Bell margin rim, where fine tentacles root into the mesoglea

parts.notes: Numerous short, fine tentacles (roughly 80 to 100 on an adult, count approximate and not verified) bearing nematocysts that catch plankton. Feeding category, since their function is prey capture. Their individual size is tiny, so they are a texture-level detail. Penetration is 2 mm into the bell margin; the depth is large relative to the root radius because the root is very thin.

parts.name: Oral arms

penetration.overlap_region: Manubrium base and the central subumbrellar floor, where the arms join the manubrium

parts.notes: Four short, frilly, ruffled oral arms hang from the manubrium and carry food to the mouth. They are flexible and have no rigid joints. Feeding category, since they serve ingestion. Relative to the bell they are small and do not extend far below the margin. length_m is an estimate.

parts.name: Manubrium and mouth

penetration.overlap_region: Central subumbrellar cavity, the apex of the core bell

parts.notes: Central, four-lobed mouth at the tip of the manubrium, a short tube hanging from the subumbrella. Axial and single, so symmetry is centre. No PolyForge equivalent for a mouth on a radial body; mouth_snout is the nearest but does not fit.

parts.name: Rhopalia (marginal sensory bodies)

penetration.overlap_region: Rhopalial niche at the bell margin rim

parts.notes: Small club-shaped marginal sense organs with statoliths for balance and light-sensing eyespots. They sit in niches at the margin. Eight in Aurelia (count from general knowledge, not verified in session). Fixed to the margin. Sensory category. No direct PolyForge equivalent (eye_bead is the closest sensory shape but does not match).

parts.name: Gonads (horseshoe-shaped)

penetration.overlap_region: Subumbrellar floor, in four horseshoe-shaped pockets

parts.notes: Four horseshoe-shaped reproductive gonads visible through the translucent bell, often coloured. Reproduction does not fit any of the five categories. They are placed under aesthetics as non-functional for locomotion, sensing, feeding or manipulation, and this is a judgement call. Flag for the schema owner.

parts.name: Gastrovascular radial canals
parts.order: 4-fold gastric pouches, with radial canals extending to the margin

penetration.overlap_region: Fully internal to the core bell; no surface mesh needed

parts.notes: Internal digestive network (gastric pouches and radial canals) that distributes food through the bell. It is visible only as faint lines through the translucent bell. It is listed for completeness and has no external mesh. Feeding category, since it is digestive.

constraints.symmetry: Radial (4-fold and 8-fold) about the vertical +Y axis, not bilateral. PolyForge's bilateral spine sweep cannot express this directly.
constraints.gait: Bell pulsation (jet propulsion). The coronal muscle contracts the margin rhythmically; appendages trail passively. Hydrostatic, with no rigid joints.
other: Apply the normalized frame as given: +Y is the swimming direction (bell apex), x and z span the bell, y in [0,1] with 0 at tentacle tips.
Bell-to-appendage attachments are soft, so use hydrostatic joints. Rigid joints would misrepresent the body.
Coordinates assume a bell 0.25 m across and 0.10 m tall including tentacles. Tentacle and arm lengths are estimates.

library_gaps.why: PolyForge body is a bilateral spine sweep. Parts cannot be placed around a central axis without a radial-array primitive.

library_gaps.feature: Translucent gelatinous bell as the core
library_gaps.why: The core is a flattened dome of mesoglea, not a bilateral spine. No library shape matches an umbrella-shaped core.
The contractile muscle is a continuous ring around the bell margin, not a discrete limb or part.
A dense ring of fine tentacles needs an instancing or array primitive. Individual parts are too small to model one by one.
None of the five categories is reproductive, so gonads are forced into aesthetics.
No PolyForge sensory part is a marginal club on a rim. eye_bead is the nearest and does not fit.

library_gaps.feature: Manubrium mouth on a radial body
library_gaps.why: mouth_snout and mouth_jaws assume a bilateral head with a front face, not a central mouth on an underside.
